alternatives.argument: Step 1.1 proves sqrt(t) is absolutely continuous by splitting the interval family at a cutoff, with separate bounds for short and longer horizons; it also computes the unbounded second derivative. Step 1.2 proves the Caputo kernel product is integrable at each t by bounding each half interval with an L1 factor. Step 2.1 uses the C1 Lebesgue change-of-variables theorem under Countable Choice to evaluate the Beta integral and obtains Gamma(3/2). Step 3.1 computes the uniform first-step error and proves it is not O(h^(3/2)); step 4.1 computes the graded first node. No global graded-mesh rate is claimed.

The item defines the exact general-grid L1 weights, recurrence, input domain and failure statuses. Its weight formula is integrated analytically and makes no use of the composite midpoint or Simpson error bounds.

The proof establishes AC, identifies each secant-slope average using the CC Riemann–Lebesgue bridge, cancels the zero-mean panel error against the midpoint kernel, bounds the last panel directly, sums earlier panels and applies the proved discrete comparison bound.
